unit.why: A halakhic and custom discussion about not studying Mishnah on the night of Shavuot, which contains a first-person memorate of the author's debate with his uncle R. Zvi and the uncle's concession the following year.
unit.boundary_note: Part of a numbered series of glosses (לה) on Shavuot-night customs. The previous and next divisions are related teachings, not continuations of this story.

stories.start_quote: וכבר בימי חורפי הי' לי פתחון פה
stories.end_quote: שלא יעיינו כלל במשניות בלילה זאת
stories.summary_en: As a young man the author argued with his uncle and teacher R. Zvi that one may not study Mishnah on Shavuot night; the uncle did not agree, but on the eve of Shavuot the next year he conceded with a shining face and said he had already warned his disciples.

tags.why: The whole matter concerns the night of Shavuot.

quotes: וכל אחד למוד תורה שבע״פ לפי השגתו
שלשים שנה למדתי ואמרתי משניות בלילה הקדושה
tags.why: The subject is what to study on Shavuot night.

quotes: ופלפלתי עמו הרבה בחכמה שאסור לומר
tags.why: A halakhic and custom question is debated and decided.

quotes: איבד זכותי שאסור לומר וללמוד משניות כדברך
tags.why: The prohibition on studying Mishnah that night is at issue.
The dispute is between the young author and his uncle and master.
The master concedes to his young disciple and admits he lost merit.

quotes: שלשים שנה למדתי ואמרתי משניות בלילה הקדושה דשבועות איבד זכותי
tags.why: The uncle belatedly recognises that his long-held practice was wrong.

quotes: על מאמר הזוה״ק דבעי לי׳ למילעי בהאי לילא
tags.why: The story is framed by exegesis of a Zohar passage.
The short narrative is wrapped in an extended halakhic and homiletic frame.

quotes: והי' זה ביום שבת שבלילה הי' ליל שבועות
tags.why: The first debate took place on the Sabbath, as a passing setting.
